newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean consul killed in Russia.
newsitem.headline: South Korean consul killed in Russia.

text.p: A South Korean diplomat in Russia's Far East city of Vladivostok was found bludgeoned to death outside his apartment, the Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
Ministry spokesman Suh Dae-won declined all comment on South Korean media reports suggesting that North Korea was behind the killing on Tuesday of consul Choi Duck-keun.
Choi was responsible for North Korean affairs and security at the consulate, which has a staff of five diplomats.
"He was killed on the stairs of his apartment building by unidentified men," Suh said.
"What we know officially from our investigations is that he was hit on the head by a very heavy tool," he said. His wallet, passport, cash and other personal belongings remained untouched.
Suh said Choi had also been stabbed in the stomach.
State radio had reported that Choi may have been stabbed by a poison needle, but Suh said the puncture mark was much larger than a needle wound.
The radio quoted a Russian witness as saying two Asian men were lurking in the stairwell before Choi entered the building.
South Korean diplomats have been warned to take extra precautions following a threat by North Korea to retaliate unless South Korea returned a submarine that intruded into the South two weeks ago.

Pyongyang has demanded the immediate return of the vessel along with its surviving and dead crew. The submarine landed an estimated 26 North Koreans, of whom 22 have been killed and one captured alive during a manhunt.
"Speculation had it that Choi might have been murdered by North Koreans especially in consideration of the fact that he was in charge of North Korean affairs," Yonhap said.
Another Foreign Ministry official said security at foreign missions had been increased following the killing.
"We have immediately instructed all overseas missions to step up security measures and take precautions against any possible terrorist attacks," he said.
Choi was transferred to Vladivostok in 1995 from the consulate in Kiev, where his son now attends university. His wife was with him in Vladivostok. A daughter lives in Seoul.
There is a small community of South Korean businessmen living in Vladivostok, mostly working in trading and shipping firms. A number of North Koreans also live in the port city.
